studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 — Merck/Moderna five-year topline press release, 20 January 2026
studies.draft_uses: The draft's correction log states this document 'is still in nothing we hold' and that a one-sided nominal p=0.0075 figure attributed to it 'stays out.' The draft body does NOT print p=0.0075.
studies.latest_known: The Merck/Moderna press release of 20 January 2026 is publicly available and explicitly reports RFS HR=0.510 (95% CI 0.294–0.887) and one-sided nominal p=0.0075. This document exists and is indexed. The draft's correction log incorrectly implies uncertainty about whether the document exists. However, since the draft body does not use p=0.0075, no body-text figure is wrong. The correction log's characterisation of the document as unverifiable is itself inaccurate — the document is publicly available at the Merck newsroom and on Nasdaq — but this is a correction-log error, not a stale-figure error in the article body.
studies.what_changed: The draft's correction log says the January 2026 topline document 'is still in nothing we hold' and that p=0.0075 'stays out until somebody produces it.' The document is publicly available and does report one-sided nominal p=0.0075 alongside HR=0.510 (0.294–0.887). The draft body correctly omits p=0.0075 (it is not a figure the body uses), but the correction log's stated reason — that the document cannot be found — is factually wrong. This is a SUPERSEDED finding in the correction log, not in the article body. Editors should note the document exists and is findable; the correction log should be updated to reflect that the figure was removed for a different reason (e.g., the peer-reviewed JCO paper is the preferred citation) rather than because the source document cannot be located.

The Lancet paper prints two-sided p=0.053 for the same data, which the draft correctly explains. No newer version of this release exists.
studies.what_changed: No figures changed. The draft correctly attributes one-sided p=0.0266 to this release and two-sided p=0.053 to the Lancet paper, and correctly explains the relationship between them.

studies.latest_known: Merck/Moderna press release 19 August 2026, confirmed by multiple independent sources (ASCO Post, OncLive, CancerNetwork, Dermatology Times, BioPharm International, Targeted Oncology, ecancer, KOL Pulse, AJMC). studies.name: Adjuvant PD-1 inhibitor overall survival in melanoma — background claim
studies.draft_uses: Claim that 'no randomised trial against placebo has reported a statistically significant overall survival benefit as a prespecified endpoint in its own population' for adjuvant PD-1 inhibitors in melanoma
studies.latest_known: A 2026 European Journal of Cancer nationwide registry-based study (published December 2025) found no OS benefit from adjuvant therapy in stage III melanoma in a real-world population, consistent with the draft's claim. The EORTC 1325/KEYNOTE-054 OS data are anticipated in late 2026 per that same paper but have not yet been published as of 2 September 2026. The draft's claim is specifically about prespecified endpoints in randomised trials vs placebo — the registry study is observational and does not contradict it; the KEYNOTE-054 OS readout, if published, could change this claim. As of 2 September 2026, no such publication has been identified.
studies.what_changed: No published randomised trial vs placebo has reported a statistically significant prespecified OS benefit for adjuvant PD-1 inhibitors in melanoma as of 2 September 2026. The KEYNOTE-054 OS readout is anticipated but not yet published. If it publishes before the draft's next update, this claim will require revision.

objections.objection: The draft describes the Phase 3 as 'blinded against the assessment bias the earlier one carried' but the Phase 3's primary endpoint is also investigator-assessed, a fact the draft itself acknowledges two paragraphs later — making the framing in the 'Why the blinding row matters' section internally inconsistent.
objections.quote: It is the more trustworthy trial by a wide margin — seven times larger, and blinded against the assessment bias the earlier one carried.
objections.why: The draft correctly notes elsewhere that INTerpath-001's primary endpoint is 'recurrence as assessed by the investigator.' Saying the Phase 3 is 'blinded against the assessment bias the earlier one carried' overstates the correction: the double-blind design reduces directional bias but does not eliminate investigator assessment. The draft's own later paragraph says exactly this. The sentence as written contradicts the body's more careful treatment of the same point, and the changelog even records a prior correction of 'exactly' this language.
objections.fix: Change to: 'blinded against the directional pull that assessment bias carried in the open-label trial' — or simply cross-reference the caveat that follows two paragraphs later rather than implying the bias is fully removed.

objections.objection: The draft calls KEYNOTE-942 'an open-label study of 157 patients, not the blinded study of 1,137 that was announced' — the contrast implies the Phase 3 is blinded in a way that directly addresses the open-label weakness, but the Phase 3's primary endpoint is also investigator-assessed, so the contrast is sharper than the facts support.
objections.quote: the numbers carried in the coverage — the 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death, the 59% reduction in the hazard of distant metastasis or death, both from the five-year follow-up — describe a different trial: an open-label study of 157 patients, not the blinded study of 1,137 that was announced.
objections.why: Calling INTerpath-001 simply 'the blinded study' in direct contrast to the 'open-label' Phase 2b implies the blinding fully resolves the assessment-bias problem. The draft's own later section acknowledges the Phase 3 endpoint is still investigator-assessed. The short version, read alone, leaves a misleading impression that the two trials differ on this dimension more completely than they do.
objections.fix: Add a parenthetical: 'the double-blind study of 1,137 that was announced (whose primary endpoint is also investigator-assessed, though the blinding substantially limits directional bias).'

objections.objection: The draft attributes a specific argument to Morning Glory Sciences — that absolute recurrence risk is lower in stage IIB/IIC patients so 'the same hazard ratio delivers a smaller absolute benefit' — but then describes Morning Glory Sciences as 'the English edition of a non-English industry site, which we cite for an argument we have checked ourselves rather than on its standing,' which is an unsupported characterisation of the outlet's nature and standing.
objections.quote: Morning Glory Sciences — the English edition of a non-English industry site, which we cite for an argument we have checked ourselves rather than on its standing
objections.why: Describing Morning Glory Sciences as a 'non-English industry site' whose standing is insufficient to cite on its own is a characterisation of a third party's credibility and editorial nature. No evidence is offered for this description. If Morning Glory Sciences is a legitimate specialist outlet, this framing is unfair to them and potentially misleading to readers about the quality of the source.
objections.fix: Either remove the parenthetical characterisation of the outlet's standing entirely, or replace it with a factual description that can be verified — e.g. its country of origin and publication type — without the editorial judgment about its standing.

objections.objection: The draft states the Phase 3 trial enrolled 'Stage IIB–IV' patients and that the upper end 'did not move: stage IV was in both,' but the KEYNOTE-942 registry and Lancet paper describe its population as stage IIIB–IV, not stage III–IV, meaning the upper bound comparison is correct but the characterisation of what 'did not move' should specify IIIB–IV to IV, not III–IV.
objections.quote: The upper end did not move: stage IV was in both.
objections.why: This sentence is accurate as far as it goes — stage IV was indeed in both trials. However, the surrounding sentence says the Phase 3 'widened it downward — adding IIB, IIC and IIIA below the earlier trial's floor of IIIB.' IIIA is listed as newly added, which is correct per the registry (KEYNOTE-942 enrolled IIIB–IV; INTerpath-001 enrolled IIB–IV including IIIA). The sentence about the upper end not moving is fine, but the claim that IIIA is newly added deserves a source check — the ASCO abstract for INTerpath-001 confirms stage IIB, IIC, III, or IV, and KEYNOTE-942 enrolled IIIB–IV, so IIIA is indeed newly included. This is accurate and not an error, but the phrasing 'the upper end did not move' could be read as implying stage III was in both, when KEYNOTE-942's floor was IIIB. This is a minor precision issue, not a material error.
objections.fix: No change required; the sentence is accurate. Flag resolved.

objections.objection: The draft states the five-year topline of 20 January 2026 reporting a one-sided nominal p = 0.0075 'is still in nothing we hold' and 'stays out' — but CancerNetwork and Targeted Oncology both report this figure (HR 0.510; 1-sided nominal P = 0.0075) attributed to a Merck press release of January 20, 2026, which is publicly available and cited in specialist coverage the draft itself holds.
objections.quote: We also removed a 'five-year topline of 20 January 2026' reporting a one-sided nominal p = 0.0075. That document is still in nothing we hold and in no source list on this page, and nothing found since has changed that. It stays out until somebody produces it.
objections.why: The p = 0.0075 figure appears in CancerNetwork (citing 'Merck. January 20, 2026') and in Targeted Oncology, both of which are specialist outlets the draft holds or cites. The draft's own source list includes the ASCO Post's coverage of the five-year data. The January 20, 2026 Merck press release is publicly available and cited in the specialist literature. Saying the figure 'exists in nothing we hold' and keeping it off the page when it is verifiable from sources the draft already uses is an error of omission that could mislead readers about the evidentiary basis for the p-value, and it contradicts the draft's own standard of tracing every number to a company release or peer-reviewed paper.
objections.fix: Obtain the January 20, 2026 Merck press release (publicly available; cited by CancerNetwork and Targeted Oncology), add it to the source list, restore the one-sided nominal p = 0.0075 to the page with correct attribution, and remove the correction notice claiming the figure is unverifiable.

objections.objection: The draft says 'the release says so' when describing that the hazard ratios in the announcement belong to KEYNOTE-942 — this is accurate — but then says 'No hazard ratio, no confidence interval, no p-value and no percentage describing the size of that effect' for the Phase 3, which is correct, yet the scorecard section says 'data support scores 1 — the rubric's anchor for 1 is purely qualitative assertion with no numeric support' — the Phase 3 announcement does contain the qualitative result that both endpoints were met as 'statistically significant and clinically meaningful,' which is more than purely qualitative assertion with no numeric support, even if no effect size is given.
objections.quote: Data support scores 1 — the rubric's anchor for 1 is purely qualitative assertion with no numeric support, which is what a statement that two endpoints were met, with no figure for either, is.
objections.why: The draft's own changelog records a prior correction: 'We had scored data support 1 against the rubric's anchor of "no data cited," when a directional result was cited and what is absent is magnitude.' The current text still equates 'met its endpoints' with 'purely qualitative assertion with no numeric support.' A threshold crossing at a prespecified interim analysis is a directional result with implicit statistical content (the threshold was crossed), not a purely qualitative assertion. The draft's own earlier correction acknowledged this distinction and then re-introduced the same conflation.
objections.fix: Revise to: 'Data support scores 1 because the rubric's lowest anchor applies when no effect size — no hazard ratio, interval, or percentage — has been released; a statement that a threshold was crossed is directional but carries no magnitude, and magnitude is what this dimension measures.'

objections.objection: The draft says 'Most specialist outlets attributed the earlier trial's figures correctly' and then names six outlets — but it also says 'An earlier version of this sentence named OncLive and FierceBiotech when we held neither' and that FierceBiotech 'we still do not hold' — meaning the claim that 'most' outlets attributed correctly is based on a sample that excluded at least one outlet (FierceBiotech) the draft acknowledges it cannot assess.
objections.quote: Every outlet whose article we hold attributed those figures correctly to KEYNOTE-942 — The ASCO Post, Dermatology Times, Practical Dermatology, KOL Pulse, MLQ News and OncLive
objections.why: The claim 'every outlet whose article we hold' is accurate and appropriately scoped. However, the lead sentence of the section says 'Most specialist outlets attributed the earlier trial's figures correctly' — a broader claim than 'every outlet we hold.' The draft cannot establish what outlets it does not hold did. 'Most' implies a representative sample; the sample is self-selected by what the publication could obtain.
objections.fix: Change 'Most specialist outlets' to 'Every specialist outlet whose coverage we hold' to match the scoped claim that follows.

objections.objection: The draft says the Phase 3 is 'double-blind, placebo-controlled, so nobody assessing a recurrence knows which treatment produced it' — but the Phase 3 is placebo- AND active-comparator-controlled, meaning the comparison arm receives pembrolizumab plus placebo, not pembrolizumab alone; the blinding is between vaccine and placebo, not between treatment and no treatment.
objections.quote: It is double-blind and placebo-controlled, so nobody assessing a recurrence knows which treatment produced it.
objections.why: This is accurate in its essential claim — the assessor is blinded — but 'placebo-controlled' alone understates the design. The trial is placebo- and active-comparator-controlled: both arms receive pembrolizumab; the experimental arm adds intismeran and the control arm adds placebo. The sentence is not wrong but is incomplete in a way that could mislead a reader into thinking the control arm receives no active treatment, which matters for interpreting the result.
objections.fix: Change to: 'It is double-blind and placebo-controlled — both arms receive pembrolizumab; the experimental arm adds intismeran and the control arm adds matched placebo — so nobody assessing a recurrence knows which treatment produced it.'

objections.objection: The draft's 'What is established' section states 'Any-grade immune-related adverse events were similar — 45.2% on the combination versus 44% on pembrolizumab alone' and then says 'Reading only the first pair would tell you the added therapy costs nothing, and it does' — the final clause 'and it does' is ambiguous and could be read as saying the added therapy does cost nothing, the opposite of the intended meaning.
objections.quote: Reading only the first pair would tell you the added therapy costs nothing, and it does.
objections.why: The sentence is grammatically ambiguous. 'And it does' most naturally reads as confirming the preceding clause — i.e., 'the added therapy costs nothing' — which is the opposite of what the draft intends. The intended meaning is that the added therapy does carry a cost (grade 3+ events at 25% vs 18%). A reader who stops at this sentence takes away the wrong conclusion about safety.
objections.fix: Rewrite as: 'Reading only the first pair would tell you the added therapy costs nothing in toxicity — but it does carry a cost: grade 3 or worse events were higher.'

objections.objection: The draft describes the scoring formula for 'Is the effect real?' as '(3×.25 + 4×.20 + 4×.15 + 5×.10 + 5×.10) ÷ .80' but the six dimensions listed are Source quality 3, Data support 1, Reproducibility 4, Consensus 4, Recency 5, Rigor 5 — the formula omits Data support (weight .20) from the numerator and the denominator is .80 rather than 1.0, which implies Data support is excluded from this sub-score, but the text does not say so explicitly in the formula line itself.
objections.why: The formula is internally consistent — five dimensions at weights .25+.20+.15+.10+.10 = .80, with Data support excluded and scored separately — but a reader checking the arithmetic will find only five terms in the numerator against six listed dimensions and no explanation within the formula line of why Data support (scored 1) is absent. The rubric section says 'only one of the six dimensions, data support, asks whether an effect size exists at all, so the magnitude score rests on that dimension alone' but this explanation appears after the formula, not beside it.
objections.fix: Add a parenthetical immediately after the formula: '(Data support excluded from this sub-score; it is the sole input to the magnitude score below.)'

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly stated that the Phase 2b was open-label in stage IIIB–IV, that the Phase 3 adds stage IIB/IIC node-negative disease, that the Phase 3 HRs have not been disclosed and therefore the 157-patient figures 'cannot be placed alongside the 1,137-patient result' and 'belong to the Phase 2b population, not to this one.' Also noted the double-blind design eliminates open-label assessment bias as an explanation for the directional result, while correctly flagging that magnitude cannot be assessed.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not explain the width of the OS confidence interval (0.165–1.345) or the n=14 death count underlying it, does not discuss the one-sided vs two-sided p-value framing, and does not give the absolute RFS or OS landmark rates that would let a reader feel the size of the Phase 2b effect.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated plainly and in its own words that 'The companies did not disclose hazard ratios, absolute event rates, P values, or other phase 3 efficacy estimates in the topline announcement.' Attributed the 49%/59% figures to the KEYNOTE-942 five-year follow-up. Noted the trial will continue to evaluate OS.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the OS confidence interval width or the n=14 death count, no explanation of what a hazard ratio measures versus a headcount, no note on the open-label design of the Phase 2b versus the blinded Phase 3, and no discussion of the population difference (stage IIB/IIC newly included).

best_coverage.got_right: Stated that 'Detailed phase 3 efficacy metrics (e.g., HRs) were not disclosed; OS and other secondary endpoints remain immature.' Attributed the 49%/59% figures to the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 five-year data. Correctly described the trial as double-blind with 1,137 patients randomised 2:1.
best_coverage.still_omitted: No discussion of the OS interval width or the death count behind it, no explanation of the open-label versus blinded design difference between the two trials, no note on the population expansion to stage IIB/IIC, and no discussion of what 'met its endpoint' does and does not convey about effect size.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated that 'The companies have not disclosed the Phase 3 hazard ratios, p-values, median follow-up or detailed adverse-event rates.' Noted that the stock moves 'came before the companies disclosed the detailed efficacy and safety data needed for regulatory, clinical and payer review.' Cited an ASCO discussant (Grant McArthur) who said Phase 2 results alone were insufficient to change clinical practice and noted the Phase 3 covers a broader population including stage II disease.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not enumerate confidence intervals or event counts as missing (the draft's quoted version of the MLQ sentence includes these; the actual text does not). No discussion of the OS interval width, the n=14 death count, the open-label versus blinded design distinction, or the one-sided/two-sided p-value issue.

best_coverage.got_right: Explicitly listed what was not disclosed: 'The Phase 3 hazard ratios, confidence intervals, absolute RFS and DMFS rates, subgroup analyses, and detailed safety results have not yet been reported.' Stated that OS 'does not yet demonstrate an overall survival benefit' and that 'longer follow-up will be required to determine whether the reduction in recurrence and distant metastasis ultimately translates into improved survival.' Noted that interpretation will require assessment of absolute benefit, toxicity, discontinuation, and quality of life — not just relative RFS/DMFS. Correctly attributed the 49%/59% figures to the Phase 2b.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not explain the OS confidence interval width or the n=14 death count, does not discuss the open-label design of the Phase 2b as a limitation on the figures being cited, and does not address the one-sided/two-sided p-value distinction or the population difference between the two trials.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated explicitly that 'The companies released no effect sizes, no hazard ratios and no survival curves' and that 'Overall survival data are still being collected.' Explained that the Phase 2b confidence interval on the RFS hazard ratio 'ran from 0.294 all the way to 0.887' because the trial was small (n=157), and that 'the data were compatible with a halving of risk, and also with a fairly modest benefit.' Correctly attributed the Phase 2b figures to KEYNOTE-942.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not discuss the OS confidence interval (0.165–1.345) or the n=14 death count, does not address the open-label versus blinded design distinction, does not discuss the population expansion to stage IIB/IIC, and does not explain the one-sided/two-sided p-value framing.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated that 'the companies have not yet disclosed the magnitude of benefit, hazard ratios, event rates, or detailed safety findings.' Noted that 'High-risk resected stage IIB/IIC melanoma carries recurrence and melanoma-specific mortality comparable to stage III' — the counter-argument to the lower-absolute-benefit concern. Listed remaining readouts including 'absolute benefit, stage/biomarker subgroup effects, discontinuation and feasibility metrics, and overall survival.' Attributed the 49%/59% figures to the KEYNOTE-942 five-year update.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not discuss the OS confidence interval width or the n=14 death count, does not address the open-label design of the Phase 2b as a limitation, and does not explain the one-sided/two-sided p-value distinction.

best_coverage.got_right: Stated that 'numerical efficacy estimates, confidence intervals, follow-up duration, and detailed subgroup findings were not disclosed.' Noted that 'detailed efficacy and safety data, overall survival results, presentation at a medical meeting, and regulatory review will be necessary before its potential clinical role can be fully established.' Correctly described the trial as enrolling 1,137 patients.
best_coverage.still_omitted: Does not attribute the 49%/59% figures to the Phase 2b at all — they are not mentioned — so the substitution problem the draft identifies is avoided by omission rather than by explicit attribution. No discussion of OS interval width, n=14 death count, open-label design difference, or p-value framing.

contradictions.quote: MLQ News: The companies have not disclosed hazard ratios, confidence intervals, p-values, median follow-up or event counts for the Phase 3 trial.
contradictions.counterexample: MLQ News actually states: 'The companies have not disclosed the Phase 3 hazard ratios, p-values, median follow-up or detailed adverse-event rates.' The words 'confidence intervals' and 'event counts' do not appear in the MLQ text found; the draft's quoted version adds two items MLQ did not enumerate.
contradictions.fix: Quote MLQ only for what it actually said: that hazard ratios, p-values, median follow-up, and detailed adverse-event rates were not disclosed. The confidence-interval and event-count items in the quoted sentence belong to the draft's own analysis, not to MLQ, and should be attributed accordingly.

contradictions.quote: One detail has had little attention. Merck's own description of the Phase 3 defines its primary endpoint as recurrence 'as assessed by the investigator' rather than by central adjudication.
contradictions.counterexample: The ASCO Post explicitly states: 'The primary endpoint was recurrence-free survival, defined as the time from randomization to any disease recurrence... as assessed by the investigator, or death due to any cause.' Cancer Therapy Advisor states the same language verbatim. Both pieces published this detail at the time of the announcement.
contradictions.fix: Reframe as: 'The investigator-assessed endpoint definition appeared in the ASCO Post and Cancer Therapy Advisor, though neither piece discussed what it implies about assessment bias in the context of the double-blind design.' The claim of 'little attention' is overstated; the detail was printed, just not analysed.

contradictions.quote: Every outlet whose article we hold attributed those figures correctly to KEYNOTE-942 — The ASCO Post, Dermatology Times, Practical Dermatology, KOL Pulse and MLQ News
contradictions.counterexample: OncoDaily, Biotech Blueprint, AJMC, CancerNetwork, BioPharm International, EMJ Reviews, and Pharmacy Times also attributed the figures correctly to KEYNOTE-942 (or omitted them entirely). The list of five outlets understates the breadth of correct attribution and could imply the others did not get it right.
contradictions.fix: Expand the list or use a formulation such as 'every specialist outlet we reviewed' rather than naming only five, to avoid implying the unnamed outlets failed on attribution.

contradictions.quote: The third figure has not come back. We also removed a 'five-year topline of 20 January 2026' reporting a one-sided nominal p = 0.0075. That document is still in nothing we hold and in no source list on this page, and nothing found since has changed that.
contradictions.counterexample: The January 20, 2026 Moderna/Merck press release is publicly available (Moderna IR PDF, s2.q4cdn.com) and reports 'one-sided nominal p=0.0075' for the five-year KEYNOTE-942 RFS analysis. CancerNetwork also cites this p-value from the five-year data. The document exists and is findable; the draft's correction notice implies it may not.
contradictions.fix: The correction note should be updated: the January 20, 2026 release exists and is publicly available. The p=0.0075 figure is real and sourced. The draft should either add this document to its source list or explain why it is choosing not to rely on it, rather than leaving a reader to infer the document may be fictitious.

coverage.what_this_piece_can_add: No outlet found — including the most careful specialist treatments — explains the OS confidence interval (0.165–1.345) in terms of what its two ends mean in plain language, or connects the n=14 death count to the interval width in a way a non-specialist reader can use. The draft's walk-through of that interval, and its explanation of why 'an encouraging trend' is the only honest label for a result that spans an 84% reduction to a 35% increase, is genuinely absent from all coverage found and is the layer this piece adds that even the best specialist reporting does not.
